summary: Describes what the IETF actually is: an organization defined by its participants and processes, not by a formal membership or legal entity. Earlier documents used the term without defining it. It is a Best Current Practice.

eli5.summary: People kept saying the IETF without saying what it is. This explains that it is a group of people who work together, not a company you join.

subtitle: A short note that finally says what 'the IETF' means: an open community, not a company or a club with formal membership.

tldr.problem: Many RFCs say 'the IETF' as if it were a defined thing, but no IETF document actually defined it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes the IETF as an open global community of network designers, operators, vendors and researchers, and points to BCP 9, BCP 10 and BCP 11 for how it works.
tldr.outcome: It is a Best Current Practice (BCP 58) that gives a single reference definition: the IETF is an unincorporated, freestanding organization, partially supported by the Internet Society.

today: RFC 3233 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 58), and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Definition Was Needed
sections.content:
Many RFCs refer to the IETF, and many important IETF documents speak of it as if it were already defined. The abstract points out the gap: no IETF document correctly defines what the IETF is. This short Best Current Practice fills it.

Even the main document on the standards process, BCP 9 (RFC 2026), never defines the IETF.
sections.eli5: Everyone used a name but nobody wrote down what it meant. This note writes it down.

sections.title: What the IETF Is
sections.content:
Following BCP 11 (RFC 2028), the Internet Engineering Task Force is an open global community of network designers, operators, vendors and researchers. They produce technical specifications for the evolution of the Internet architecture and the smooth operation of the Internet.

The RFC is explicit that the IETF is not a corporation. It is an unincorporated, freestanding organization. There is no board of directors, no formally signed bylaws and no treasurer. Its structure, including its leadership, working groups and the definition of IETF membership, is described in BCP 11, and the procedures for choosing leadership are in BCP 10 (RFC 2727).

So when RFCs say 'the IETF', they mean the group that acts in accordance with BCP 9, BCP 10 and BCP 11.
sections.eli5: It is like a huge neighbourhood club that anyone can join in, with no president's office or bank account of its own. The rules for how it works are written in other documents.

sections.title: The IETF and the Internet Society
sections.content:
The IETF is partially supported by the Internet Society (ISOC), an international non-profit organization incorporated in the US. ISOC has thousands of individual and corporate members who pay membership fees, and it provides services to the IETF such as insurance and some financial and logistical support.

Internet standardization is an organized activity of ISOC, and the ISOC Board of Trustees ratifies the procedures and rules of the standards process. Even so, the IETF is not a formal subset of ISOC. For example, one does not have to join ISOC to be a member of the IETF.
sections.eli5: A helper group pays for the club's insurance and helps with the paperwork, but you can be in the club without joining the helper group.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC notes that all IETF protocols must describe the security aspects of the environment in which they will be used, and that the IETF has a Security Area that discusses the security of its protocols. Descriptive documents such as this one, however, do not affect the security of the Internet.
sections.eli5: This note only describes a group, so it cannot make the internet any safer or less safe.
